seedTerms: A loved one being put in harm's way

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: High-Society Revenge
jokes.joke: I once dated a socialite, and after we broke up she got revenge the rich-person way. She didn’t key my car or spread rumors. She changed my seat at a charity gala so I spent three hours next to a man explaining his wine portfolio. Halfway through, I was begging her to just slash my tires.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Understudy for Revenge
jokes.joke: My ex cheated on me, so I spent a year plotting revenge. Elaborate revenge. I researched his new girlfriend's schedule, his gym hours, his mom's birthday. But I'm so indecisive I couldn't commit to a plan. Slash his tires? Text his mother? Get a better haircut and 'accidentally' walk by? I ended up doing all three, on different days, like a part-time villain. Closure isn't a moment for me, it's a rollout schedule.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Front Row Drama
jokes.joke: My partner took twenty minutes pacing in the performing arts theater lobby just trying to pick between sparkling water and tap, absolutely paralyzed by the menu. Then, ten seconds after the live play started, during an actor's quiet dramatic whisper, they confidently decided it was the perfect time to open a family-sized bag of SunChips.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Parking Spot Payback
jokes.joke: I planned the perfect revenge on the guy who stole my parking spot. Key the car? Egg it? Leave a nasty note under the wiper? Being indecisive, I stood there fifteen minutes trying to decide. He came back, saw me hovering, and asked if I needed help finding my keys. Now he waves every time he sees me. My revenge is having to wave back like we're friends.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Balcony Justice
jokes.joke: I dated this socialite who loved making dramatic entrances—balconies, spotlights, the whole thing. One night she dumped me right before her big charity gala, so I showed up anyway. When she stepped onto the balcony to greet everyone, I yelled, “Your Wi‑Fi still auto-connects to my phone!” The gasp from the crowd was priceless. That’s the closest I’ve ever come to feeling powerful in loafers.

scores.comment: Clear escalation and a solid rollout-schedule tag, though the indecisive revenge premise and villain framing feel somewhat familiar.
Strong behavioral reversal from trivial indecision to disastrously confident timing; concrete, relatable, and cleanly staged.
The accidental-friendship turn is genuinely non-obvious, and the forced waving back makes an effective final escalation.
The Wi-Fi reveal is unexpected but not consequential enough to justify the gala setup, and the loafers tag adds flavor more than laughter.
Clean premise, strong escalation, punchline lands via understatement.
